question_text: What are the best PCB layout techniques to minimize capacitive and inductive crosstalk between traces?
answer_text:
1) Increase the spacing between traces (e.g., the "3W rule").
2) Route adjacent layers perpendicularly (orthogonal routing).
explanation_text: Doubling the distance between traces drastically cuts the parasitic electric and magnetic fields. If you must route signals on adjacent internal layers, run them at 90-degree angles to each other to minimize the overlapping parallel length. Also, bringing the reference ground plane closer to the traces tightens the fields, reducing crosstalk.
bonus_question_text: What is the "3W Rule" in PCB layout?
bonus_answer_text: A best practice stating the distance between the centers of two parallel traces should be at least three times the trace width (3W) to keep crosstalk to an acceptable minimum.
